lt-1.1.summary: Phase 1 (Settings and the queue). Settings for `landing.trains` and the machine keys, with validation. See LT15, LT7.3; §D16.
acceptance: Tests in `src/app/test/integrator-trains-config.test.mjs` load a valid file and get every default; refuse an unknown key, each out-of-range value, `minBranches` above `maxBranches`, a target without `policy`, a `regenerate` rule without `command`, a needed platform with neither an environment nor `ci.workflow`, and `machine.*` or `lease.*` in `.avoozl.json`, each message naming the key and file; a gated target with a CI-only platform loads with the extra-run warning; a target override replaces the `trains`-level key.

lt-1.2.summary: Phase 1 (Settings and the queue). Batch branches and queue registration. See LT1.1, LT1.2, LT1.3, LT1.4, LT1.5, LT16.1; §D2, §D3.
acceptance: Tests in `src/app/test/landing-batch-branches.test.mjs`: a verified task's commit appears on the bare remote as `avoozl-batch/<task>` and in the queue with every field; a planted content-rule match blocks the push; `submit` refuses a wrong prefix, a task outside an approved plan and a failed cheap check, each naming the step; a descendant requeue keeps `seq`; a rewritten head is refused with the reason and the remote branch and entry are unchanged; a branch built on another queued branch records it in `builtOn`.

lt-1.3.summary: Phase 1 (Settings and the queue). CI guidance for repositories and setup's workflow check. See LT1.7, LT1.8; §D17.
acceptance: A setup test with three fixture workflows (no filter, `branches: [main]`, `branches: ['**']`) lists the first and third with the right line each and not the second; the workflow files are byte-identical after the run; `node scripts/release-scan.mjs` is clean on the new doc.

lt-2.1.summary: Phase 2 (The landing lease and the integrator). One lease module from the activity lease. See LT3.2; §D5.1.
acceptance: `src/report.test.mjs`'s activity tests pass unchanged; new tests in `src/lease.test.mjs` cover take on none and on stale, busy on active foreign, renew and end with the right and the wrong lease ID, and a 180-second lease going stale at 181 seconds.

lt-2.2.summary: Phase 2 (The landing lease and the integrator). The landing lease: compare-and-set, heartbeat, expiry and the hung holder. See LT3.1, LT3.3, LT3.4, LT3.5, LT3.9; §D2, §D5.2.
acceptance: Tests in `src/app/test/landing-lease.test.mjs`: two stores on one database file race to take the lease and exactly one wins, the other gets `busy` and writes nothing; a lease renewed on time stays; one not renewed for three heartbeats goes stale; a stale lease with a live pid is refused with one Needs you item across three loops; a stale lease with a dead pid is taken.

lt-2.3.summary: Phase 2 (The landing lease and the integrator). The integrator process and role. See LT2.1, LT2.2, LT2.3, LT2.5; §D4, §D21.
acceptance: Tests: with a `train` target, a tick that verifies a task pushes only the batch branch and never the trunk; the integrator process is the only caller that pushes the trunk (a test wraps git and records pushes by process); the supervisor restarts a killed integrator; `status --json` shows holder, train and trigger state.

lt-2.4.summary: Phase 2 (The landing lease and the integrator). A taker cleans up a dead train. See LT3.6, LT3.7; §D5.3.
acceptance: Tests kill an integrator (a) mid-stack, (b) mid-full-validation under gated and (c) after an optimistic push; in each the taker leaves no landing worktree, runs the fake cleanup command once, frees the slot, and (a, b) requeues members in the same order or (c) runs full validation on the pushed head before forming a new train.

lt-p1.summary: Phase 2 (The landing lease and the integrator). Proof: one integrator per trunk, and a dead one clears by itself. See LT2, LT3; §D5.
acceptance: Expected: (1) one train, one trunk push; the other integrator reports `busy`; (2) the survivor takes the lease after three missed heartbeats, cleans up and lands the three; (3) nothing is taken and one Needs you item names the hung integrator; (4) the push is refused, the stack is rebased and rechecked, and the trunk never shows a forced update.
Expected result observed; receipt under `docs/evidence/`.

lt-3.1.summary: Phase 3 (The train engine). Train records and the back-to-back trigger. See LT4; §D2, §D6.
acceptance: Tests with a fake clock: two ready entries with `minBranches` 3 wait until `maxWaitMinutes` and then go as a train of two; twelve ready entries make a train of ten and leave two; a train finishing starts the next only after the cooldown; a paused entry and an entry whose `builtOn` is queued outside the train are not ready, each with its hold reason; no two trains exist for one target at any step.

lt-3.2.summary: Phase 3 (The train engine). Stacking with the cut rule. See LT5; §D7, §D21.
acceptance: Real-git tests: B built on A, both queued, stack A then B with each of A's commits exactly once; B built on A where A landed yesterday, B's commits only; B built on A where A is queued outside the train, B held naming A; a branch whose commits are all in the trunk is closed as contained; every stacked commit has its trailer and original author; `src/app/test/landing-trains.test.mjs` passes unchanged.

lt-3.3.summary: Phase 3 (The train engine). Mechanical conflicts with per-file verification; semantic ones go to the later task. See LT6.1, LT6.2, LT6.3, LT6.5, LT6.6; §D8.
acceptance: Real-git tests: two appends to a `union` path stack cleanly; a `regenerate` rule's command rewrites a lockfile and it is staged; a rule whose `verify` fails leaves the file unstaged and the conflict semantic; with no rules every conflict is semantic; the later of two branches editing the same lines is dropped and its chat gets the file list and commit, while a third, unrelated member still lands; a planted rerere record is not replayed.

lt-4.1.summary: Phase 4 (Validation and local capacity). Machine platform environments and the platforms a train needs. See LT7.3, LT7.4; §D9.1, §D9.2.
acceptance: Tests: a classifier fixture script gets the changed paths and its JSON output decides the platforms; rules map `src/win/**` to `windows-x64` only; a classifier that exits nonzero or prints bad JSON fails the train's step with the reason; a platform environment set in `.avoozl.json` is refused.

lt-4.2.summary: Phase 4 (Validation and local capacity). Cheap and full validation runners with suite results. See LT7.1, LT7.2, LT7.5, LT7.6; §D9.3.
acceptance: Tests with fake wrapper scripts: the wrapper receives the command and runs in the landing worktree; a cheap check failure stops before any push; a timeout fails with "timed out after N s"; a results file's suites appear per platform on the train; a missing or malformed results file means whole-command reruns, recorded once.

lt-4.3.summary: Phase 4 (Validation and local capacity). Local resource slots shared across workspaces. See LT13.1, LT13.2, LT13.3; §D14.
acceptance: Tests: two workspaces on one machine database, one `windows-vm` slot: the second train waits until the first ends; a worker check waits with "waiting for windows-vm (train-…)"; a crashed holder's slot is freed by the taker (with lt-2.4).

lt-4.4.summary: Phase 4 (Validation and local capacity). CI fallback for platforms without a local environment. See LT7.7; §D9.3.
acceptance: Fake-GitHub tests: a gated train with a CI-only platform dispatches exactly one run naming every CI-only platform, waits for it, counts as validated only on success, and deletes the ref; an optimistic train makes no dispatch and reads the push's run.

lt-4.5.summary: Phase 4 (Validation and local capacity). Avoozl's own `test.yml` accepts the validation dispatch. See LT8.8; §D16.1.
acceptance: A test reads `test.yml` and finds the input, `push` on `main` only, the job `test` with matrix `os` values unchanged, and the platform-to-runner mapping above; one dispatch run on a scratch branch with `platforms=linux-x64,windows-x64` runs only those two legs, linked in the pull request; the scratch branch is deleted afterward.

lt-5.1.summary: Phase 5 (Landing). Gated and optimistic policies, the guarded push, a moved trunk, and no force push anywhere. See LT8.1, LT8.2, LT8.3, LT8.4, LT8.5, LT3.8, LT3.10, LT16.2, LT16.3, LT16.4, LT16.6, LT16.7; §D10.1, §D10.2, §D10.3, §D10.4.
acceptance: Real-git tests: gated pushes only after full validation passes and never on a failure; optimistic pushes after cheap checks and then runs full validation on the pushed head; a train with tasks of two drivers writes two intents, both read back before the push; a trunk moved during the train is rebased onto and pushed after rechecks, and after `maxRebases` moves the train fails with "trunk kept moving" and members requeue; a batch branch pushed to during the train is kept and its new head queued; no push in any test is forced; a test scanning every `git push` argv in `src/` finds no `--force`, `-f`, `--force-with-lease` or `+` refspec.

lt-5.2.summary: Phase 5 (Landing). Watch the train's one CI run. See LT8.6, LT8.7, LT4.6; §D10, §D9.3.
acceptance: Fake-GitHub tests: the run ID and conclusion land on the train record; a train with a CI-only platform is validated only after the run passes; with `waitForLastTrain` false the next train starts before the conclusion and with true it waits; Stop the line counts only validated trains' heads.

lt-p2.summary: Phase 5 (Landing). Proof: ten branches land in one train. See LT1, LT4, LT5, LT6, LT8; §D7, §D10.
acceptance: Expected: one train of nine; the later of the two same-line branches returns to its task with the conflicted file and the earlier commit; the stacked branch carries no duplicated commit; the changelog merges by rule and passes verify; one trunk push, one CI run, no forced update on any ref; the returned branch, fixed by a merge and requeued, lands in the next train.
Expected result observed; receipt under `docs/evidence/` with the train timeline.

lt-6.1.summary: Phase 6 (Failure). Flaky reruns and the boundary bisect over failing suites. See LT10.1, LT10.2; §D11.1.
acceptance: Tests with a fake suite runner: a suite that fails then passes is recorded `flaky` and the train continues; in a train of ten with member 7 bad the bisect probes at most four boundaries, each probe runs only the failing suite on the failing platform, and names member 7; with no results file each probe runs the whole command; every probe passing names the last member and records the interaction.

lt-6.2.summary: Phase 6 (Failure). Land the good branches; return, eject, revert or fix forward. See LT10.3, LT10.4, LT10.5, LT16.5; §D11.2.
acceptance: Real-git tests: gated with one culprit lands nine and returns one; gated with a second culprit after the first restack stops at `maxBisects`; optimistic `revert` leaves the trunk green with one revert commit and no forced update; `fix-forward` opens a stop and a fix task first in line; `return` sends the excerpt and counts rounds, then ejects; `eject` opens one Needs you item; a `direct` repository still halves.

lt-p3.summary: Phase 6 (Failure). Proof: a red train lands the rest. See LT10; §D11.
acceptance: Expected: gated: the flake is recorded and ignored; the bisect probes only the failing suite on the failing platform and names member 5; seven land; member 5's chat gets the suite and excerpt. Optimistic: eight land, then one revert of member 5's range turns the trunk green; member 5 is returned. Neither run forces any ref.
Expected result observed; receipt under `docs/evidence/`.

lt-7.1.summary: Phase 7 (Queue depth and wait). Queue depth and time in queue on the Landing queue page, the CLI and MCP. See LT14.1, LT14.3; §D15.
acceptance: A seeded-store test checks depth, each time in queue and hold reason, and the running train's step; a counting-client test shows zero GitHub calls for the page, the CLI and the MCP read; the UI test renders the page at 390 and 1280 px; screenshots in light and dark go to the owner (R92.12).

lt-p4.summary: Phase 7 (Queue depth and wait). Proof: a live train on Nupp. See LT1, LT7, LT8, LT13.1, LT13.2; §D20.
acceptance: Expected: no branch waits for its own CI run; each train ends with one CI run on the trunk; median time in queue under 30 minutes; any red train is narrowed to one branch and the rest land.
The owner records the day's queue depth and time-in-queue numbers from the Landing queue page in a receipt under `docs/evidence/`.

lt-8.1.summary: Phase 8 (Review pull requests). Review pull requests only on request. See LT1.6, LT9.1; §D3.
acceptance: A fake-GitHub test shows no pull request for a queued task until `review` runs, one after it, the same one on a second run, and the number on the queue entry; a test over the tick path counts zero pull request creations.

lt-8.2.summary: Phase 8 (Review pull requests). Comment on and close review pull requests after landing. See LT9.2, LT9.3; §D10.4.
acceptance: Fake-GitHub and real-git tests: after a landed train the pull request has one comment with the train link, position and trunk commit link, passes the privacy rule, and is closed; the batch branch's remote head is unchanged from queue time until its deletion; a closed pull request gets no comment; no push in the test targets the batch branch.

lt-9.1.summary: Phase 9 (Reaping and the rest of visibility). The reaper. See LT11, LT16.6; §D12.
acceptance: Tests: an entry idle past `idleHours` gets one Needs you item across three loops; an entry 51 commits behind is refreshed and rechecked, its `refreshed` range is recorded, its remote batch branch still shows the original head, and the local ref is on no remote; the next train stacks from the refreshed range; a conflicting one goes back to its task; a fully contained entry is closed with the commit and its branch deleted; an orphan remote batch branch is listed once and still exists afterward; a second pass with nothing changed writes nothing.

lt-9.2.summary: Phase 9 (Reaping and the rest of visibility). The rest of the queue numbers, and the wait alert. See LT14.1, LT14.2, LT14.4; §D15.
acceptance: A seeded-store test checks every number; a counting-client test shows zero GitHub calls; the alert fires once for an entry over the threshold and not again; the UI test renders the page at 390 and 1280 px; screenshots in light and dark go to the owner (R92.12).

lt-p5.summary: Phase 9 (Reaping and the rest of visibility). Proof: nothing sits silently. See LT11, LT14; §D12, §D15.
acceptance: Expected: each case ends in its D12 state with one Needs you item where D12 says so; no batch branch on the remote moved; the page and `landing status --json` show the same numbers; the wait alert fired once per entry over the threshold.
Expected result observed; receipt under `docs/evidence/`.

lt-10.1.summary: Phase 10 (Scheduling and CI capacity). Conflict-aware train composition by footprint. See LT12; §D13.
acceptance: Tests: with entries A, C, D, B where A and B overlap, `same-train` makes the order A, B, C, D; with `maxBranches` 2 it makes A, B; `serialize` makes A, C, D and leaves B; an entry whose real diff exceeds its declared paths is matched on the real files.

lt-10.2.summary: Phase 10 (Scheduling and CI capacity). CI capacity for fallback runs. See LT13.4; §D14.
acceptance: Fake-GitHub tests: with `capacity.ci.macos-arm64` 2 and two macOS jobs queued the train waits and its step says so; with one queued it dispatches; the read count per loop is one.

lt-11.1.summary: Phase 11 (The resolver chat and the red-CI bisect). The integrator resolver chat, off by default. See LT2.4, LT6.4; §D4, §D8.
acceptance: A fake-executor test: the chat is opened only for a covered file whose rule failed, never for an uncovered one; its brief holds no push, pull request or comment instruction and passes `briefAllowed`; a resolution that fails `verify` is not staged and the conflict returns to the later task.

lt-11.2.summary: Phase 11 (The resolver chat and the red-CI bisect). Bisect when CI goes red on a landed trunk. See LT10.6; §D11.3.
acceptance: Fake-GitHub tests: a failed run on a train's head bisects locally and reverts or fixes forward per settings before the next train starts; a failed run on a head no train pushed changes nothing; the CI-only-platform case opens one Needs you item with the failing jobs; with the setting off nothing happens.
